claims.claim_text: The Republican Party characterizes the 2012 U.S. administration's handling of immigration cases as defying the asserted right of U.S. states and the federal government not to recognize same-sex relationships licensed in other jurisdictions.

The Republican Party characterizes the 2012 U.S. administration's federal personnel benefits as defying the asserted right of U.S. states and the federal government not to recognize same-sex relationships licensed in other jurisdictions.

The Republican Party characterizes the 2012 U.S. administration's allowance of a same-sex marriage at a military base as defying the asserted right of U.S. states and the federal government not to recognize same-sex relationships licensed in other jurisdictions.

The Republican Party characterizes the 2012 U.S. administration's refusal to defend the Defense of Marriage Act in court as defying the asserted right of U.S. states and the federal government not to recognize same-sex relationships licensed in other jurisdictions.

The Republican Party assesses the 2012 U.S. administration's opposition to the asserted governmental nonrecognition principle for same-sex relationships as inconsistent with the president's inaugural oath.
Republicans reaffirm support for a U.S. constitutional amendment defining marriage as the union of one man and one woman.
Republicans support campaigns in several additional U.S. states to constitutionally define marriage as the union of one man and one woman.
Republicans commend the U.S. House of Representatives for defending in court laws preserving governmental authority not to recognize same-sex relationships licensed in other jurisdictions.
Republicans commend U.S. state attorneys general for defending in court laws preserving governmental authority not to recognize same-sex relationships licensed in other jurisdictions.
Republicans applaud citizens in the majority of U.S. states for enshrining the one-man-and-one-woman definition of marriage in their state constitutions.
